column1: # Mario & Luigi: Brothership: Acquire's game on Unreal Engine 4.27 (project Vermillion; IoStore, MallocBinned3), SDK 12.3.2, NVN, Wwise, Bink movies through a material; the base game, 1.0.0 (v0).
# The update in hand fails its NCA's hash check; the same sdk and movie builds as OCTOPATH TRAVELER II and TRIANGLE STRATEGY.
# Started from the NSP script's provisional profile (dm/games/profile_guess.py) and brought up on the Mac (docs/agents)

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The game sets near-zero NVN depth (nvnDeviceSetDepthMode); offline pipeline bases use main0_z.
# The game's Switch device profile sets rhi.syncinterval=2 (30 fps), and the same route at 30 and at 60 fps reaches the same stages at the same times
# Speed measured at 120 against 60 over the same inputs (README.md, Frame rate)

# Unreal Engine 4.27: as OCTOPATH TRAVELER II (0100A3501946E000/game.tsv), nninitStartup needs virtual address memory and reserves a 62 GB region for the engine. The rewriter's engine-wide rules cut the
# FMallocBinned3 constructor call (the host runs Unreal's heap on a malloc zone outside the guest block; dm/tools/ue_malloc.py, hle_uemalloc.c) and give the region what the alias region has room for,
# 2.81 GB (dm/tools/ue_region.py, hle_svc.c); the SDK's node area is cut to 62 MB (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py, the SDK-wide rules on this sdk build). Alias region = node area + the region + 256 MB for
# regions made later; 256 MB stacks, 384 MB heap region
# the NPDM declares 80 MB of system resource
# The 3D pad layout (a D-pad and a right stick): the game's input config binds both (Vermillion/Config/DefaultInput.ini)
# Each material's shaders inline in its cooked package, the packages in the IoStore container (Vermillion-Switch.utoc), the global shaders in the pak: shader_split.py ue_legacy_jobs
